sources.fact: First public Microsoft acknowledgement of the Exchange Online problem: X post at 17:54:26 UTC on 12 Nov 2026 (12:54 p.m. ET), scoped to the Americas and pointing to EX1550543.

disagreements:
1) START TIME. Microsoft's own record gives three different values. (a) The header Start Time for both EX1550543 and MO1550821 now reads 10:05:00 UTC, 12 Nov (PennO365 and Cloud Admin Hub, read 17 Nov). (b) The final-status text says 'Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 4:20 PM UTC'. (c) CIO reported on 13 Nov 'The outage began at 16:17 UTC on Nov. 12, according to Microsoft's service health dashboard'.
BleepingComputer gives MO1550821's start as 1:26 PM ET (18:26 UTC); its first post was 18:27:35 UTC. No Microsoft text explains 10:05 UTC, and I could not tell when the header changed.
Outside views differ again: Al Jazeera says about 16:00 GMT (user reports); PPC Land puts network-monitor onset at about 17:30 to 17:45 UTC; AP says 'around midday Thursday in the U.S.'; ABC says the first post came 'shortly before 1 p.m. ET'.

2) END / ALL-CLEAR. (a) The record's End Time is 16:10 UTC, 13 Nov, declared retroactively in the final status at 04:15:46 UTC, 14 Nov. That same final status still says Microsoft will 'continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions'. (b) The @Microsoft post at 16:40:18 UTC, 13 Nov, says 'We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service'. (c) The X all-clear came at 06:09:51 UTC, 14 Nov. (d) AP wrote 'Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored'.
Unverified: a live page listing a final resolution update at 05:42 UTC, 14 Nov, and an Outlook.com consumer remediation at 03:51 UTC, 14 Nov. Both appear only in search summaries; I could not confirm either.

3) DURATION. Published figures conflict:
- 23 h 50 m: the record's 16:20 to 16:10 window.
- 30 h 5 m: header 10:05 to 16:10 (Cloud Admin Hub), probably the source of 'about 30 hours'.
- 36 h 15 m: first X post to X all-clear.
- 37 h 50 m: first admin-center post to X all-clear.
- Press also uses 'nearly 24 hours', 'more than a day' and '36-hour'.

4) 48-HOUR EXTENSION TIME. Microsoft's own times: MO1550821 at 09:03:36 UTC, X at 09:24:08 UTC, EX1550543 at 09:55:42 UTC. Secondary times: 'about 09:10 UTC' (a search summary), 12:00 UTC (PPC Land via Observador), and BleepingComputer's 8:05 AM ET (13:05 UTC) update, which reflects reporting lag.

5) 'NORMAL LEVELS'. The 'approaching normal levels' wording appears at 14:01:18 UTC (EX), 14:01:51 UTC (MO) and 14:17:29 UTC (X). Do not mix it up with the 09:03 and 09:55 UTC updates, which say capacity 'has not yet returned to normal levels'.

6) CHANGE CORRELATION (Microsoft contradicts itself). On X at 20:19:33 UTC, 12 Nov: 'We've not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact'. In MO1550821 at 01:12:07 UTC, 13 Nov: 'we've begun reverting a recent network configuration change that correlates with the start of impact'.

7) CAUSE FRAMING EVOLVED.
- 13 Nov: 'an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change'.
- 14 Nov preliminary root cause: 'traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug' in the systems that establish connections.
- 16 Nov, Lamanna: three factors. First, a latent lock-contention defect from 'a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers'; the July 2026 date is ITPro and UC Today paraphrase. Second, extra load from a Teams failover about 15 hours earlier. Third, about 14% of gateway capacity was out from an unrelated issue the previous day.
Microsoft never says how the 'network capacity upgrade' relates to the July gateway fix. Separately, the 12 Nov line 'elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic' sits uneasily with Lamanna's 'increased load' from failover; that is a load shift, not traffic growth, but The Conversation questioned it.

8) MALICIOUS-ACTIVITY WORDING DRIFTED.
- 03:34:14 UTC EX and 03:36:01 UTC MO: 'no indication this is the result of malicious activity'.
- Lamanna at 03:37:28 UTC adds 'or cyber'.
- MO at 04:56:39 and 09:03:36 UTC: 'not aware of any malicious activity'.
- From 12:18 UTC (MO) and 15:53:37 UTC (EX): 'no evidence of malicious activity'.
- 16:40 UTC: 'not related to cyber or AI / agents'.
- Lamanna at 22:02 UTC: 'not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling'.
The Register reportedly noted the hedging; I did not read it.

9) ATTRIBUTION. 'We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day...' is an @MSFT365Status post at 15:39:30 UTC. NBC (10:15 AM EST entry, which is earlier) and BleepingComputer (12:06 PM ET update) present it as a Lamanna statement. ABC7NY gives his 'Our teams are reviewing...' with no time.

10) APOLOGY WORDING. The admin center (17:57:06 UTC) says 'caused you and your business'. The @Microsoft X post (16:40:18 UTC) says 'caused our customers and partners'.

11) 'ANY REGION' TIME. The decoded X time is 18:07:33 UTC (1:07 p.m. ET). WindowsForum cites Mashable at 1:45 p.m. ET and puts an X acknowledgment with Americas wording at 10:08 a.m. PT (18:08 UTC), but the Americas post decodes to 17:54:26 UTC.

12) PIR NAMING. The admin center says 'A post-incident report has been published' (04:46 and 04:47 UTC, 16 Nov). X calls it the 'Preliminary Post-Incident Report' (05:48 UTC). A final PIR was promised 'within five business days' of 14 Nov. Reports on 15 Nov that no PIR existed are consistent with the 16 Nov release.

13) TEAMS. Microsoft records TM1550488 (14:45 to 15:53 UTC, resource contention) as separate, and some outlets fold it into the outage. Lamanna's Teams failover about 15 hours before the outage is a different event by time. Microsoft has not linked the two.
